# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L274-L326


# Vulnerability details

## Summary

The operatorDelegator, integral to handling transactions with EigenLayer—from deposits to withdrawals—facilitates the queueWithdrawals function for initiating withdrawals. However, due to a flaw in a function responsible for returning the value of tokens within the operatorDelegator, the TVL is miscalculated, creating an opportunity for users to illicitly extract funds.

## Vulnerability Detail

the function `getTokenBalanceFromStrategy` is used to get the token balance of a operatorDelegator, which is important for tvl calculation:
```solidity=327
function getTokenBalanceFromStrategy(IERC20 token) external view returns (uint256) {
        return
=>            queuedShares[address(this)] == 0
                ? tokenStrategyMapping[token].userUnderlyingView(address(this))
                : tokenStrategyMapping[token].userUnderlyingView(address(this)) +
                    tokenStrategyMapping[token].sharesToUnderlyingView(
                        queuedShares[address(token)]
                    );
    }
```

it basically queries the strategy for each token in eiganLayer and gets how much tokens are deposited there. it uses the queuedShares mapping to tell it how many shares have been queued for withdrawal and to add them, because as you queue a withdrawal in eiganlayer, shares arent giving to you directly there is a withdrawal period.

it's stored like this 
```solidity=232
queuedShares[address(tokens[i])] += queuedWithdrawalParams[0].shares[i];
```

but as we can see in `getTokenBalanceFromStrategy` at line 537 it used erroneously queuedShares[address(this)] instead of the token. 
and because queuedShares[address(this)] is always 0 , it always thinks it never has any shares queued , making it reort less token amounts when there is actively queuing shares. 
this allows a malicious user to steal funds from other restakers  risk free, by frontrunning queued shares with a withdrawal and then afterwards depositing the same funds to get more ezETH.

## Proof Of Concept

- attackScenario
    - Assumptions:
        - there are 10 users each with 10 ezETH 
        - there is 100 stETH in the protocol
        - STETH:ETH = 1:1
        - a operatorDelegator submtted a transaction to withdraw 20 stETH
        - Bob is one of the 10 users
    1. Bob sees the `queueWithdrawals` transaction and frontruns it calling withdraw 10 ezETH, basically locking him at 10stETH after the cooldown period.
    2. afterwards the call to queueWithdrawals executes, and now the tvl is wrongly set to 80stETH instead of 100 until the withdrawal completes
    3. Bob deposits 10stETH (not necessarily the one he withdrew if the cooldown period is longer than eiganlayer) getting 10*totalSupply(ezETH)/totalTVL = 10*90/80 = 11.25 ezETH
    4. afterwards the admin calls completeQueuedWithdrawal to complete the wthrawal and bring back the tvl to 100ETH
    5. now bob owns 11.25 instead of 10 while not depositing any more stETH than the other users, he effectivley now owns 11.25 stETH instead of 10 stETH
    6. basically there is a free arbitrage to happen by anybody and the bigger the share of the pool he deposits after the queuewithdrawal the bigger he is going to steal form other users

## Impact

steal of user funds

## Code Snippet

## Tool used

Manual Review

## Recommendation

```diff=329
- queuedShares[address(this)] == 0
+  queuedShares[token] == 0
```


## Assessed type

Context

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L279-L313


# Vulnerability details

## Summary

the function `WithdrawQueue:claim` is responsible for completing withdrawals and sending users their funds,the function uses transfer() to send ether to the user instead of call. There are a number of issues with using transfer(), as it can fail for a number of reasons , and if it fails it will make the user's funds locked.

## Vulnerability Detail

the function `claim` uses transfer instead of call:
```solidity=302
if (_withdrawRequest.collateralToken == IS_NATIVE) {
            payable(msg.sender).transfer(_withdrawRequest.amountToRedeem);
        }
```

which could fail for a number of reasons but most important of which are any changes or forks in ethereum that result in higher gas fees than transfer provides will make the function revert.

the revert will basically lock the user's eth in the contract unable to be withdrawn because calls to it would revert in the transfer call.

## Tool used

Manual Review

## Recommendation

use call instead of transfer in `claim`:

```solidity=302
if (_withdrawRequest.collateralToken == IS_NATIVE) {
    (bool success, ) = payable(msg.sender).call{value : _withdrawRequest.amountToRedeem}("");
    require(success, "error");
        }
```



## Assessed type

DoS

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L491-L576


# Vulnerability details

## Summary

The protocol uses the restakeManager for depositing funds and minting ezETH in a manner similar to ERC4626 vaults. However, it lacks protections against flashloan attacks, allowing early depositors to manipulate exchange rates and effectively steal funds from later depositors.

## Vulnerability Detail

The stakeManager:deposit function facilitates the deposit of a supported LST (liquid staking token) in exchange for ezETH, calculating the mint amount based on the protocol's current value, new contributions, and existing ezETH supply. The formula used mirrors that of an ERC4626 vault, determining mint amounts proportionally to the contributed value relative to the total assets under management:
```solidity=123
function calculateMintAmount(
        uint256 _currentValueInProtocol,
        uint256 _newValueAdded,
        uint256 _existingEzETHSupply
    ) external pure returns (uint256) {
        // For first mint, just return the new value added.
        // Checking both current value and existing supply to guard against gaming the initial mint
        if (_currentValueInProtocol == 0 || _existingEzETHSupply == 0) {
            return _newValueAdded; // value is priced in base units, so divide by scale factor
        }

        // Calculate the percentage of value after the deposit
        uint256 inflationPercentaage = (SCALE_FACTOR * _newValueAdded) /
            (_currentValueInProtocol + _newValueAdded);

        // Calculate the new supply
        uint256 newEzETHSupply = (_existingEzETHSupply * SCALE_FACTOR) /
            (SCALE_FACTOR - inflationPercentaage);

        // Subtract the old supply from the new supply to get the amount to mint
        uint256 mintAmount = newEzETHSupply - _existingEzETHSupply;

        // Sanity check
        if (mintAmount == 0) revert InvalidTokenAmount();

        return mintAmount;
    }
```

This mechanism, though standard, is susceptible to manipulation by malicious actors who can inflate the _currentValueInProtocol. This value is derived from the calculateTVL function, which aggregates the value of assets held by operator delegators, plus those in the deposit and withdrawal queues:

```solidity=355
totalTVL += (address(withdrawQueue).balance + totalWithdrawalQueueValue);
```

A malicious user can exploit this by donating assets to the withdrawal queue, thereby inflating the totalTVL. and in doing so infaltes the price of ezETH to make next users deposits round down in favor of him.

## Proof Of Concept

- assumptions:
    - their are no funds in the protocol , totalTVL = 0
    - steth is a supported LST
    - Bob is a malicious user and he sees Alice transaction to deposit 10 stETH
- attack scenario:
    1. Bob frontruns alice by calling `stakeManager:Deposit` and deposits 1 wei of stETH
    2. according to the calculation in `renzoOracle:calculateMintAmount` he will get minted 1 wei of ezETH
    3. Bob sends 5.1e18 stETH to the withdrawalQueue which gets added to the totalTVL .
    4. now the exchange rate of ezETH/stETH = totalTVL/totalSupply(ezETH) = 5.1e18 + 1/1 = 5.1e18 stETH for 1 wei of ezETH
    5. Alice transaction goes through, and this is how much she will be minted: 
        - inflationPercentaage = (1e18 * _newValueAdded) /
            (_currentValueInProtocol + _newValueAdded) = 10e18*1e18/(10e18+1+5.1e18) = 0.621e18
        - newEzETHSupply = (1 * 1e18) /
            (1e18 - 0.66e18) =  2.6392.639 = 2 (rounds down)
        - mintAmount = newEzETHSupply - _existingEzETHSupply = 2 - 1 = 1
    6. so alice gets minted 1 wei ezETH.
    7. Bob and alice hold the same amount of ezETH so they each own 50% of the tvl in the protocol. tvl = 5.1e18 + 1 + 10e18 = 15.1e18 + 1.
    8. bob owns = 7.55 stETH and alice holds 7.55stETH
    9. so bob stole from alice 2.45 stETH

## Impact

early depositor would be able to steal funds from later depositers.

## Tool used

Manual Review

## Recommendation

- Implement slippage controls that allow users to specify a minimum amount of ezETH they expect to receive for their deposit.
- Set a minimum deposit value to reduce the impact of small, manipulative deposits.
- Seed new stakeManagers with an initial TVL to stabilize the initial exchange rates and prevent manipulation by the first few depositors.


## Assessed type

ERC4626

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L274-L326


# Vulnerability details

## Summary

The function stakeManager:calculateTVLs plays a critical role in determining the Total Value Locked (TVL) within the protocol, influencing the amount of ezETH users receive for their deposits and the valuation of their withdrawals. a flaw in the price oracle integration leads to inaccurate TVL reporting, which could result in significant financial discrepancies for users.

## Vulnerability Detail

The stakeManager:calculateTVLs function is designed to aggregate the TVL from various sources within the protocol, including operator delegators, deposit queues, and withdrawal queues. The calculation for the withdrawal queue is particularly problematic:

```solidity=316
if (!withdrawQueueTokenBalanceRecorded) {
                    totalWithdrawalQueueValue += renzoOracle.lookupTokenValue(
=>                        collateralTokens[i],
                        collateralTokens[j].balanceOf(withdrawQueue)
                    );
                }
```

This code segment attempts to determine the value of assets held in the withdrawal queue by querying the balance of each supported token (collateralTokens[j]) and evaluating its worth in terms of ETH. However, due to a critical oversight, the oracle fetches the price using collateralTokens[i] as the reference token instead of collateralTokens[j]. This misalignment between the queried token and the token for which the balance is checked results in a value calculation based on the wrong price.

The error in using collateralTokens[i] for collateralTokens[j]'s value could lead to the TVL being reported as either overvalued or undervalued, depending on the relative prices of the tokens involved. For instance, if the price of collateralTokens[i] is higher than that of collateralTokens[j], the computed TVL will be undervalued, and vice versa.

## Proof Of Concept

This flaw in the TVL calculation leads to potential financial imbalances and can be exploited as demonstrated in the following scenario:

- Attack Scenario
    - assumptions:
        - stETH/ETH = 1:1
        - wbETH/stETH = 2:1 (just for easy calculations)
        - the collateralTokens array = [stETH,wbETH]
        - withdrawal queue is empty 
        - there are 2 depositers each deposited 10e18 stETH and have 10e18 ezETH
    1. Alice comes and deposits 10e18 wbETH, she gets 20e18 ezETH, but the withdrawal buffer is empty so 10wbETH goes to the withdrawal queue
    2. Bob deposits after alice 10e18 stETH , the tvl calculation is 20ETH + renzoOracle.lookupTokenValue(
                       collateralTokens[i],
                        collateralTokens[j].balanceOf(withdrawQueue)
                    ) = lookupTokenValue(stETH,10) = 10ETH = 30ETH
    3. so bob gets 10 * totalSupply(ezETH)/tvl = 10*40/30 = 13.3333e18 
    4. as we can see bob gets more than the first two depositers although he gave the ame amount effectively stealing from other users.


## Impact

The incorrect calculation of TVL due to the bug directly impacts the fair distribution of ezETH among users, leading to potential losses for some while unfairly benefiting others. This flaw undermines the protocol's integrity, causing trust issues and financial discrepancies that can deter user participation and investment.

## Tool used

Manual Review

## Recommendation

```diff=317
totalWithdrawalQueueValue += renzoOracle.lookupTokenValue(
-                        collateralTokens[i],
+                        collateralTokens[j],
                        collateralTokens[j].balanceOf(withdrawQueue)
                    );
```


## Assessed type

Context

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Bridge/L2/Oracle/RenzoOracleL2.sol#L50-L58


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Chainlink recommends that all Optimistic L2 oracles check with the Sequencer Uptime Feed to ensure that the sequencer is live/not down before trusting the data returned by the oracle. This check is not  implemented in `RenzoOracleL2.sol:getMintRate()` function where the data from the oracle is used. 

`RenzoOracleL2:getMintRate()` is supposed to be used during ezETH minting process on L2s as seen in `xRenzoDeposit.sol: _deposit()`. This can cause stale data values to be used during a deposit() if the chainlink sequencer feed is inactive.

More information on chainlink-L2 Sequencer feed here -> https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/l2-sequencer-feeds#overview

## Proof of Concept
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Bridge/L2/Oracle/RenzoOracleL2.sol#L50C1-L57C6

```
     * @notice Pulls the price of ezETH
     * @dev reverts if price is less than 1 Ether
     */
    function getMintRate() public view returns (uint256, uint256) {
        (, int256 price, , uint256 timestamp, ) = oracle.latestRoundData();
        if (timestamp < block.timestamp - MAX_TIME_WINDOW) revert OraclePriceExpired();
        // scale the price to have 18 decimals
        uint256 _scaledPrice = (uint256(price)) * 10 ** (18 - oracle.decimals());
        if (_scaledPrice < 1 ether) revert InvalidOraclePrice();
        return (_scaledPrice, timestamp);
    } 
```

in the above snippet we can see that a call is made to the chainlink oracle on the L2 without a check to see if sequencer is active as recommended by [chainlink](https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/l2-sequencer-feeds#example-code). This can cause stale data which may look correct to be used in the function logic. 


## Tools Used
manual review 
## Recommended Mitigation Steps

check for if the sequencer is live/active before using the data. Here is an example as recommended by the chainlink docs -> https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/l2-sequencer-feeds#example-code


## Assessed type

Oracle

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L592-L594
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RateProvider/BalancerRateProvider.sol#L28-L32
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L214-L218


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The calculated **TVL** would be incorrect.
This incorrect calculation would have spillover effect in following places.

Below is the called places and how the TVL is used.

RestakeManager - [deposit](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L499-L504) -- Determine which operator delegator to use. Also Calculate how much ezETH to mint.

RestakeManager - [depositETH](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L592-L595) - Enforce TVL limit if set and Calculate how much ezETH to mint.

BalancerRateProvider- [getRate](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RateProvider/BalancerRateProvider.sol#L29-L32) - to calculate the current rate of ezETH in ETH.

WithdrawQue - [withdraw](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L216-L218) - Calculate amount to Redeem in ETH

Since the TVL value is incorrect, this would be used in above places which again would lead to invalid result.

## Proof of Concept

Lets see, how the function is [calculateTVLs](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L274-L278) calculating the TVL.

-- iterates through operator delegators.
For each delegator, it calculates TVL for each token they hold:
-- gets the balance of each token.
-- uses an Oracle contract (renzoOracle) to fetch the token's value and calculates the TVL for the token.
-- accumulates the TVL for all tokens held by the delegator.
-- calculates the TVL for native ETH held by each delegator and accumulates it.
-- accumulates the total TVL for the protocol.
-- calculates the TVL of native ETH held in the deposit queue and adds it to the total TVL.
-- calculates the TVL of native ETH held in the withdrawal queue and adds it to the total TVL.

and the bug is in below part of the codes.

```solidity
if (!withdrawQueueTokenBalanceRecorded) {
    totalWithdrawalQueueValue += renzoOracle.lookupTokenValue(
        collateralTokens[i], ------>> @@ audit find .
        collateralTokens[j].balanceOf(withdrawQueue)
    );
}
```
In this part of the code, `collateralTokens[i]` is used instead of `collateralTokens[j]` when looking up the token value. This could lead to incorrect token values being fetched, as i is the iterator for operator delegators, not tokens.

## Tools Used
Manual review, VS code

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

```solidity
if (!withdrawQueueTokenBalanceRecorded) {
    totalWithdrawalQueueValue += renzoOracle.lookupTokenValue(
        collateralTokens[j], ---->> updated line
        collateralTokens[j].balanceOf(withdrawQueue)
    );
}
```


## Assessed type

Error

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
if protocol wants to pause the **withdraw** and **claim** and carry out upgrade, the pause can not be applied effectively.

Also, when updating some of critical parameters such as cool down time, the team could pause the withdraw and redeem and update the cool down. 

## Proof of Concept

The contract has the **__Pausable_init** in initializer. But the pause and un-pause is not used anywhere in the WithdrawQueue. contract. 

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L135-L150

```solidity
    /**
     * @notice  Pause the contract
     * @dev     Permissioned call (onlyWithdrawQueueAdmin)
     */
    function pause() external onlyWithdrawQueueAdmin {
        _pause();
    }

    /**
     * @notice  Unpause the contract
     * @dev     Permissioned call (onlyWithdrawQueueAdmin)
     */
    function unpause() external onlyWithdrawQueueAdmin {
        _unpause();
    }

```

The pause and unpause functions in the contract serve as mechanisms to control the contract's functionality during exceptional circumstances or when maintenance operations are required. Here's why they are included:

**Emergency Pausing:** The pause function allows an authorized admin to halt certain functionalities of the contract in case of emergencies or unexpected issues. For example, if a critical vulnerability is discovered, pausing the contract can prevent further interactions and potential exploitation until the issue is resolved.
**Maintenance:** These functions can also be used during maintenance activities such as upgrades or fixes. By pausing the contract, developers can ensure that no new actions can be performed while updates are being applied. Once maintenance is complete, the unpause function can be called to resume normal operations.

## Tools Used

Manual review, VS code.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

if pause and unpause wanted to be used, we would suggest to apply it in the necessary functions such as withdraw or claim or in other places where the team wanted to do it.


## Assessed type

Timing

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Bridge/Connext/integration/LockboxAdapterBlast.sol#L56-L95


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The balance of [LockboxAdapterBlast](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Bridge/Connext/integration/LockboxAdapterBlast.sol#L56-L95) could be drained by specifying large extra data.

## Proof of Concept

LockboxAdapterBlast could be used to for sending assets from Ethereum mainnet to Blast and also for bridging the ERC20 assets.

the function [bridgeTo](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Bridge/Connext/integration/LockboxAdapterBlast.sol#L56-L64) would be called by the user. 

It does follwing.

**Token Resolution**: Get the addresses of the xERC20 token and its associated lockbox contract from the registry.
**Token Transfer and Approval**: Transfer ERC20 tokens from the sender to the contract and approve the lockbox contract to spend them.
**Token Deposit**: Deposit the transferred tokens into the lockbox contract.
**Approval for Bridge**: Approve the blastStandardBridge contract to spend the deposited xERC20 tokens.
**Bridge Invocation**: Call the bridgeERC20To function of the L1StandardBridge contract to initiate the token bridge operation, providing necessary parameters such as token addresses, recipient, amount, gas limit, and extra data.

The function pass the extra data which is sent by the user.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Bridge/Connext/integration/LockboxAdapterBlast.sol#L87-L94

```solidity
        L1StandardBridge(blastStandardBridge).bridgeERC20To(
            xerc20,
            _remoteToken,
            _to,
            _amount,
            _minGasLimit,
            _extraData --- @@ audit find.
        );
```

on the blast side, this _extraData  would be used to emit.

https://www.codeslaw.app/contracts/ethereum/0x7a2075519dd9598b62075fd397af0dd34b14619a#:~:text=//%20Emit%20the%20correct%20events.%20By%20default%20this%20will%20be%20ERC20BridgeInitiated,_remoteToken%2C%20_from%2C%20_to%2C%20_amount%2C%20_extraData)%3B

Malicious user could call this function with small amount and specify the large extra data. Since the lockbox call the xcontract call, it pays gas for the transaction sent.

When the extra data is big, the gas incurred could be also high.

## Tools Used

Manual review, blast bridge code flow.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

We suggest to restrict and have check on the extra data size.





## Assessed type

Error

# Vulnerability details

## Impact

The griefing attack delays the staking process, potentially causing the node to miss out on rewards or incur additional transaction costs. It also disrupts the smooth operation of the staking system.

## Proof of Concept

**1. lst Transfer to Node:**

- A certain amount of `lst` tokens is transferred to a specific node. This transfer could be part of a larger staking operation or a separate transaction.

```solidity
            strategyManager.depositIntoStrategy(tokenStrategyMapping[_token], _token, _tokenAmount);

```

**2. Expected EigenLayer Stake:**

- After receiving the `lst` tokens, the node is expected to stake them on EigenLayer. This staking process is crucial for participating in the consensus mechanism and earning rewards.

**3. Griefing Opportunity in `depositIntoStrategy`:**

- An adversary identifies an opportunity to grief the staking process by exploiting the `depositIntoStrategy` function. This function is likely responsible for handling the actual staking on EigenLayer.

**4. Dust Dropping and Front-Running:**

- The adversary drops a small amount of tokens (dust) into the pool associated with the `depositIntoStrategy` function. This dust deposit could be strategically timed to front-run a transaction submitted by the RestakeManager.

**5. Forced Asset Transfer:**

- The adversary's front-running action disrupts the staking process, forcing the node to transfer some assets back to the pool. This transfer is necessary to successfully stake on EigenLayer.



## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

- Implement mechanisms to prevent dust deposits from affecting the staking process. This could involve setting minimum deposit thresholds or filtering out dust transactions.




## Assessed type

DoS

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L327-L335


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Due to wrong check the `getTokenBalanceFromStrategy` will only return value of share not the queued withdrawal shares.
## Proof of Concept
The Protocol implement a algorithm which allows it to deposit the new assets in OperatorDelegator which does not have below the threshold allowed if there is no such a OperatorDelegator then it allows the deposit into first OperatorDelegator.
to do so it fetch the `operatorDelegatorTVLs` calculated in `calculateTVLs` function. lets have a look at the code.
1. The `calculateTVLs` get the amount of share for OperatorDelegator using `getTokenBalanceFromStrategy`
```solidity
2024-04-renzo/contracts/RestakeManager.sol:300
300: 
301:                 uint256 operatorBalance = operatorDelegators[i].getTokenBalanceFromStrategy(
302:                     collateralTokens[j]
303:                 );
304: 
305:                 // Set the value in the array for this OD
306:                 operatorValues[j] = renzoOracle.lookupTokenValue(
307:                     collateralTokens[j],
308:                     operatorBalance
309:                 );
310: 
311:                 // Add it to the total TVL for this OD
312:                 operatorTVL += operatorValues[j];
...
340:             operatorDelegatorTVLs[i] = operatorTVL;


```
`301` return the balance of `OperatorDelegator`, `306` calculate its value,  `312` add this value to `operatorTVL`, and `340` add the final value to `operatorDelegatorTVLs`. after loop got executed it returns `operatorDelegatorTVLs` which is then used to identify the right `OperatorDelegator` for deposit.
This is the purpose of `operatorDelegatorTVLs` value , let now have a look at `getTokenBalanceFromStrategy`.
2. This function is used to return the balance of strategy
```solidity
/home/aman/Desktop/audits/2024-04-renzo/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol:327
327:     function getTokenBalanceFromStrategy(IERC20 token) external view returns (uint256) {
328:         return
329:  @1>           queuedShares[address(this)] == 0 // @audit-issue : it will not work as expected
330:                 ? tokenStrategyMapping[token].userUnderlyingView(address(this))
331:                 : tokenStrategyMapping[token].userUnderlyingView(address(this)) +
332:                     tokenStrategyMapping[token].sharesToUnderlyingView(
333:                         queuedShares[address(token)]
334:                     );
335:     }
```
It check if there is any share queued for withdrawal then it also add those share and return share balance.
So now lets check where this `queuedShares` got updated.
3. When new withdrawal is queued the amount of withdrawal is added to `queuedShares` and maps to its token address.
```solidity
/2024-04-renzo/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol:232
232:  @2>           queuedShares[address(tokens[i])] += queuedWithdrawalParams[0].shares[i];
```
have a look at `@1>` and `@2>` it can be observed that the `@1>` check the `queuedShares` amount using `address(this)` which will always have `0` balance becuase `@2>` the values saved in `queuedShares` map to `token address`.

So the impact is that it will not added the values which is in `queuedShares` due to wrong map key.

## Tools Used
Manual Review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
change the if condition to fetch the `queuedShares` for the given token.
```diff
@@ -326,7 +326,7 @@ contract OperatorDelegator is
     /// @dev Gets the underlying token amount from the amount of shares + queued withdrawal shares
     function getTokenBalanceFromStrategy(IERC20 token) external view returns (uint256) {
         return
-            queuedShares[address(this)] == 0
+            queuedShares[address(token)] == 0 // @audit-issue : it will not work as expected
```


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Bridge/L2/Oracle/RenzoOracleL2.sol#L13


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
In some edge cases the Price fetch from Chainlink will be stale.
## Proof of Concept
The Protocol uses Chainlink oracle for real time price of tokens used in protocol.
There is a chance that the price return from chainlink might be stale. To prevent this case the protocol uses time window which indicates that the price return from Chainlink is either stale or not.
The Chainlink oracle used in Renzo have 84600s max-haartbeat.which meanse the price return in between `(timestamp< block.timestamp-84600s)` is a valid price rate.[check here](https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/price-feeds/addresses?network=optimism&page=1&search=cbeth)
But the Protocol add `60s` more to this window time. the Price return in this extra `60s` is not guaranteed to be correct.

## Tools Used
Manual Review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
remove `60s` time from `MAX_TIME_WINDOW`:
```diff
-    uint256 public constant MAX_TIME_WINDOW = 86400 + 60;
+     uint256 public constant MAX_TIME_WINDOW = 86400;
```


## Assessed type

Oracle

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L582

# Vulnerability details

Malicious actor can `frontrun` the deposits of an early user to `steal` his funds through `inflation attack`

//How this works(early stage)
1. Suppose a user is going to deposit `10 ether` in protocol
2. Malicious actor saw & `frontrun` this tx and `deposited` 1 wei, thus ezETHTotalSupply = 1 wei, totalTVL = 1 wei
```solidity
  if (_currentValueInProtocol == 0 || _existingEzETHSupply == 0) {
            return _newValueAdded; // value is priced in base units, so divide by scale factor
        }
```
3. Again malicious actor `directly` deposited 5 ether to depositQueue.sol, thus ezETHTotalSupply = 1 wei, totalTVL = 5 ether + 1(exclude the fee for simple)
4. Honest user `deposited` 10 ether, but got `only` 1 share[(10e18 * 1)/(5e18 + 1)] because of inflated TVL
```solidity
     uint256 inflationPercentaage = (SCALE_FACTOR * _newValueAdded) /
            (_currentValueInProtocol + _newValueAdded);

        // Calculate the new supply
        uint256 newEzETHSupply = (_existingEzETHSupply * SCALE_FACTOR) /
            (SCALE_FACTOR - inflationPercentaage);

        // Subtract the old supply from the new supply to get the amount to mint
        uint256 mintAmount = newEzETHSupply - _existingEzETHSupply;
```
5. Malicious actor `withdraw` his 1 share, which gave him `~7.5 ether` ie `50%` extra than he deposited
```solidity
  uint256 redeemAmount = (_currentValueInProtocol * _ezETHBeingBurned) / _existingEzETHSupply;
```

`Loss` of funds to early depositors

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L329


# Vulnerability details

`OperatorDelegator::getStakedETHBalance()` returns the ETH balance of an operator delegator which includes `current podOwner shares` + `stakedButNotVerified ETH` + `queued withdraw shares`
```solidity
    function getStakedETHBalance() external view returns (uint256) {
        // accounts for current podOwner shares + stakedButNotVerified ETH + queued withdraw shares
      @>  int256 podOwnerShares = eigenPodManager.podOwnerShares(address(this));
        return
           podOwnerShares < 0
              @>   ? queuedShares[IS_NATIVE] + stakedButNotVerifiedEth - uint256(-podOwnerShares)
                : queuedShares[IS_NATIVE] + stakedButNotVerifiedEth + uint256(podOwnerShares);
    }
```
`podOwnerShares` can be negative due to `share deficit`(when pod owner's ETH shares decreases between the time they queue and complete the withdrawal) 

Now the problem is, when `podOwnerShares` is negative enough(which is possible) and added to `queuedShares[IS_NATIVE]` will result in negative, which will revert the tx.(given stakedButNotVerifiedETH of that operator is 0) 
```solidity
queuedShares[IS_NATIVE] + stakedButNotVerifiedEth - uint256(-podOwnerShares)
```

## Impact
`getStakedETHBalance` has been used in `RestakeManager::calculateTVLs` and if this reverts, it will break all the core functions of the protocol like `deposit`, `withdraw` etc

## Proof of Concept
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L343
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L329

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
If `podOwnerShares` + `queuedShares[IS_NATIVE]` < 0 then return 0 ie 0 + stakedButNotVerifiedEth

Error

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L432
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Deposits/DepositQueue.sol#L163


# Vulnerability details

User `deposits` collateral token into protocol and in return receives `ezETH`, which depends on the `depositedAmount`, `ezETH totalSupply` and `totalTVL`.
 Similarly, amount of token user will receive at withdraw also depends on `withdrawAmount`, `ezETH totalSupply` and `totalTVL`
```solidity
   uint256 ezETHToMint = renzoOracle.calculateMintAmount(
            totalTVL,
            collateralTokenValue,
            ezETH.totalSupply()
        );
```
```solidity
   uint256 amountToRedeem = renzoOracle.calculateRedeemAmount(
            _amount,
            ezETH.totalSupply(),
            totalTVL
        );
```

Rewards received by protocol is deposited back through `DepositQueue::receive()`, which increases the `totalTVL` of the protocol
```solidity
   receive() external payable nonReentrant {
        uint256 feeAmount = 0;
             //Code...
        // update remaining rewards
        uint256 remainingRewards = msg.value - feeAmount;
        // Check and fill ETH withdraw buffer if required
     @>   _checkAndFillETHWithdrawBuffer(remainingRewards);

           //Code...
    }
```
Now the problem is a malicious actor can frontrun `OperatorDelegator::withdrawNonBeaconChainETHBalanceWei()`(which is withdrawing rewards from EigenLayer, which will go to rewardHandler or depositQueue) to deposit collateral token into the protocol to mint `ezETH` and withdraw `just` after reward is deposited, `stealing` other users reward.


//How this works(very simple example)
1. Suppose initial totalTVL = ezETHTotalSupply = 8 ether(simple calculation)
1. Suppose protocol receives a reward of 4 ether and its going to be deposited back
2. malicious actor saw this and frontrun this to deposit asset amount worth 2 ezETH
3. after deposit, totalTVL = 10 ether, ezETHTotalSupply = 10 ether(assume 1:1 exchange rate)
4. reward of 4 ether is deposited back, which increases the totalTVL to 14 ether but ezETHTotalSupply is still 10 ether
5. malicious actor `immediately` withdraw his 2 ezETH
6. his redeemAmount = (totalTVL * withdrawAmount)/ ezEthTotalSupply ie 14*2/10 = 2.8 ether

This `extra` 0.8 ether was honest users `reward` who were deposited their collateral since `beginning` 

## Impact
Malicious actor will steal reward of honest users

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L432

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Oracle/RenzoOracle.sol#L123-L149


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
In `RestakeManager`, functions `deposit` and `depositETH` use `RenzoOracle#calculateMintAmount` to determine how much ezETH to mint to the sender. Although there's a [check](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Oracle/RenzoOracle.sol#L146) that reverts the transaction if 0 shares are going to be minted, it is still possible to execute the inflation attack. Ideally, the attacker would need to make 1 share worth `victimsDeposit / 2 + 1`, in order to maximize victim's loss due to rounding in price calculation.

## Proof of Concept

1. Bob is about to deposit 10e18 ETH into Renzo;
2. Alice frontruns Bob with 2 transactions: She deposits 10 wei, receives 10 wei of ezETH; Then she donates 5e18 * 10 = 50e18 ETH to DepositQueue (e.g. via "selfdestructing" a contract to avoid DepositQueue [fees](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Deposits/DepositQueue.sol#L158-L183)*), so each share becomes worth (5e18 + 1) ETH;

3. Bob's deposit is executed and he receives `10e18 * 10 / (50e18 + 10) = 1` share;

4. Alice redeems back her shares and receives 54.545454545454545463e18 ETH, making 4.545e18 ETH in profit.

*`selfdestruct` reverts the state changes if it runs out of gas (but still updates the balance). As `DepositQueue#receive()` consumes too much gas to fit into selfdestruct's gas limit, the fee will not be applied.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Consider implementing virtual shares: they would absorb the donation, making the attack unprofitable; or implement slippage protection for deposits.


















## Assessed type

Other

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
`RestakeManager#calculateTVLs` is used to retrieve total value of assets in the system, denominated in ETH. However, its logic does not include RewardHandler's balance, making the ezETH price smaller than it should be (until rewards are forwarded), and enabling sandwich attacks.

## Proof of Concept

1. TVL is 100 ETH;
2. RewardHandler's balance just got updated from 0 to 9 ETH due to execution layer rewards;
3. Bob deposits 1e18 ETH into Renzo and receives 1e18 ezETH;
4. Bob sends 1 wei to RewardHandler, which sends RH balance (9 ETH) to DepositQueue; TVL becomes 110 ETH; ezETH price becomes 1.1 ETH.
5. Bob requests redemption of 1e18 ezETH;
6. After the cooldown period, Bob claims 1.1 ETH, making 0.1 ETH in profit.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Add RewardHandler's ETH balance to `totalTVL` in `RestakeManager#calculateTVLs`.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Bridge/L2/xRenzoDeposit.sol#L248


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
To ensure the price feed is not stale, both `RenzoOracle` and `RenzoOracleL2` implement the following check:
```solidity
        if (timestamp < block.timestamp - MAX_TIME_WINDOW) revert OraclePriceExpired();
```
where `MAX_TIME_WINDOW = 86400 + 60`. However, Chainlink price feeds with heartbeat of 1 day sometimes take slightly more than `86460` seconds to update. Therefore, each `deposit` or `withdraw` that would be minted in that small window (after the `86460` seconds and before the feed is actually updated) will revert, and the affected user will have to submit another transaction.

## Proof of Concept

Alice deposits 32 stETH into Renzo at t = 86472 seconds after the last CL price feed update. Her transaction reverts with `OraclePriceExpired()` and she needs to submit a new one.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Consider slightly increasing the staleness tolerance, e.g. to `1 day + 5 minutes`.

Oracle

When requesting a withdrawal, the amount of collateral that will be withdrawn is [set at the moment of request](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L242-L250), and never changes afterwards. 2. Alice requests redemption of her ezETH for a collateral token;
3. Slashing is executed;
4. While every other ezETH holder is affected by the slasing, Alice is not; and she claims her withdrawal once the cooldown period is over.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

ezETH exchange rate should be computed at the moment of claiming the withdrawal, not at the moment of request.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L362-L393


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
`RestakeManager#chooseOperatorDelegatorForDeposit` does the following:

1. iterates through OperatorDelegator's balances until there's an OD with value smaller than `TVL / 10000` 

2. If there isnt such OD, choose the first one

This approach heavily favors the first OD in the list, bringing them as much as `100% - 0.01% * (number of ODs - 1)` of deposits

## Proof of Concept

1. Let's assume there's 10 OD's in the system, and each deposit is 32 ETH.
2. First deposit of 32 ETH is sent to the first OD, second to the second OD, and so on
3. 11th deposit is sent to the first OD again
4. 12th deposit is sent to the first OD again
and so on, until there's 92 x 32 ETH deposits in the first OD

After that, OD's 2-10 will receive 1x32 ETH deposit each, after which OD#1 will be receiving next 91 deposits again.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Deposits should be allocated to the OD with the lowest TVL.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L274


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
DepositQueue is expected to receive rewards in any of the collateral tokens. They are expected to be forwarded to OperatorDelegators via `sweepERC20`.

As the collateral balances of `DepositQueue` are not included in `RestakeManager#calculateTVLs`, one can monitor `DepositQueue#sweepERC20` transactions, `deposit` before them, initiate the withdrawal right after (at a higher ezETH exchange rate), and claim it after `coolDownPeriod`, stealing rewards from honest depositors who have been holding ezETH for a significantly longer duration.

1. Alice sees a `sweepERC20` transaction in the mempool;
2. Alice deposits ETH and mints ezETH;
3. `sweepERC20` transaction is mined;
4. Alice starts a withdrawal of her ezETH at a higher price, and claims it after `coolDownPeriod`.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Include DepositQueue's balance in calculateTVL's, minus the fee that would be deduced during `sweepERC20`.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L491-L576


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
`RestakeManager#deposit` treats stETH as any other token, which is prone to the known stETH rounding issue. 

https://docs.lido.fi/token-guides/steth-on-aave-caveats/

As `RestakeManager#deposit` relies on its balance, and assumes it has received exactly `_amount` from the depositor, it then splits `_amount` into `bufferToFill` and `_amount - bufferToFill`. If `_amount` is transferred from the user to the RestakeManager with a precision loss, but both `bufferToFill` and `_amount - bufferToFill` are transferred without precision loss, the contract will not be able to execute the latter transaction, as it would own only `_amount - 1` of stETH, but would attempt to transfer `_amount - bufferToFill + bufferToFill = _amount` of stETH.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L546-L562

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Use `balanceOf(address(this))` instead of `_amount`.

The `OperatorDelegator` contract upgradeability is hindered due to the absence of the `Initializable` contract import. This prevents the proper use of the initializer function, which is essential for initializing upgradeable contracts. Without proper initialization, the contract may exhibit unexpected behavior during deployment or upgrade, potentially leading to security vulnerabilities and instability.

## Proof of Concept
Upgradeable contracts in Ethereum typically follow the pattern of separating the contract's state and logic into separate contracts. The logic contract is then made upgradeable by inheriting from the `Initializable` contract and using an initializer function to set initial state variables. However, in this case, the contract does not import the `Initializable` contract, which is crucial for initializing upgradeable contracts.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Add the import statement for Initializable from OpenZeppelin to enable proper initialization of upgradeable contracts.

```javascript
import "@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/proxy/utils/Initializable.sol";
```

Upgradable

# Vulnerability details

## Impact

The pausable functionality in `CCIPReceiver` contract current implementation lacks proper checks in the pause and unPause functions, potentially leading to security vulnerabilities and 

If the contract allows pausing even when it is already paused, it may result in unintended consequences such as redundant state changes or disruptions to normal contract operations. This can confuse users and affect the expected behavior of the contract.

Allowing the contract to be unpaused when it is not already paused can introduce security risks by potentially enabling unauthorized actions or changes to the contract state. This could lead to exploitation by malicious actors, resulting in financial losses or other detrimental outcomes.

Failure to enforce proper pausing and unpausing conditions undermines the contract owner's ability to effectively manage and control contract operations. This loss of control may lead to scenarios where critical functions are executed inadvertently or inappropriately.

```javascript
/**
     * @notice Pause the contract //@audit---info this should be unpause
     * @dev This should be a permissioned call (onlyOwner)
     */
    function unPause() external onlyOwner { //@audit----info should this contain whenNotPaused
        _unpause();
    }

    /**
     * @notice UnPause the contract //@audit---info this should be pause
     * @dev This should be a permissioned call (onlyOwner)
     */
    function pause() external onlyOwner {
        _pause();
    }
```

As it is the functions lack modifiers to prevent the functions from being called when the contract is paused or unpaused

## Proof of Concept
The `OpenZeppelin` implementation of `pausable` contracts includes specific requirements in the comments for the pause and unpause functions:

Pause Function:
According to the comments, the contract must not be paused when calling _pause.
```javascript
 /**
     * @dev Triggers stopped state.
     *
     * Requirements:
     *
@--->  * - The contract must not be paused.
     */
    function _pause() internal virtual whenNotPaused {
        _paused = true;
        emit Paused(_msgSender());
    }

   
```
Unpause Function:
As per the comments, the contract must be paused when calling _unpause.

```javascript
 /**
     * @dev Returns to normal state.
     *
     * Requirements:
     *
@--->     * - The contract must be paused.
     */
    function _unpause() internal virtual whenPaused {
        _paused = false;
        emit Unpaused(_msgSender());
    }
```

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Bridge/xERC20/contracts/optimism/OptimismMintableXERC20.sol#L11


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
`OptimismMintableXERC20` storage variables will be overridden in case its parent contract `XERC20` is upgraded.

## Vulnerability details
In order to better handle tokens bridging to different L2s, the protocol employs [the XERC20 standard, designed to make the process easier and more reliable](https://hackmd.io/@arjunbhuptani/xerc20-bridge-spec). 

[The `XERC20.sol` contract](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Bridge/xERC20/contracts/XERC20.sol#L16) has been modified to use the upgradeability pattern of OpenZeppelin.

Additionally a separate version has been created to be used on Optimism L2, called `OptimismMintableXERC20`. It inherits `XERC20.sol` and overrides some methods so that it meets the `OptimismMintable` interface required for bridging tokens by Optimism.

It also [defines 2 new variables `l1Token` & `optimismBridge`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Bridge/xERC20/contracts/optimism/OptimismMintableXERC20.sol#L11-L20):

```solidity
contract OptimismMintableXERC20 is ERC165Upgradeable, XERC20, IOptimismMintableERC20 {
    /**
     * @notice The address of the l1 token (remoteToken)
     */
    address public l1Token;

    /**
     * @notice The address of the optimism canonical bridge
     */
    address public optimismBridge;

........

}

````

And this is where the problem lies. Since `XERC20.sol` is already defined as upgradeable, it means it can change in the future and new state variables can be added.

Since `OptimismMintableXERC20` inherits `XERC20.sol` and due to the way inheritance affects storage slots if `XERC20.sol` adds a new variable it will collide with the slot of the first variable of `OptimismMintableXERC20` - `l1Token`. As a result it will overwrite it and brick token minting.


## Proof of Concept

Here is a visual explanation. I'm only including the last variable of `XERC20` since it is the important one:

#### Current storage variable layout

| XERC20   | OptimismMintableXERC20|
| -------- | ------- |
| mapping(address => Bridge) public bridges (`LAST VARIABLE`)|    |
|  | address public l1Token ( `FIRST VARIABLE`)|
|  | address public optimismBridge (`2nd VARIABLE`)|

- You can see that currently `OptimismMintableXERC20` first variable starts right after the last defined variable in `XERC20`

#### Upgraded storage layout

| XERC20   | OptimismMintableXERC20|
| -------- | ------- |
| mapping(address => Bridge) public bridges|    |
| address someNewVariable (`LAST VARIABLE`) | address public l1Token ( `FIRST VARIABLE`)|
|  | address public optimismBridge (`2nd VARIABLE`)|

- In this scenario `XERC20` adds a new address variable which as you can see from the table takes the storage slot previously used by the `l1Token` for `OptimismMintableXERC20`. Respectively `l1Token` now references the next slot for `optimismBridge` which will break the minting.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Consider using a separate storage contract just as you have done for the core Renzo contracts. This will prevent storage collisions and will allow new state variables to be safely added.

Note: Do not forget to put it as the last contract in the inheritance chain.


## Assessed type

Upgradable

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L318


# Vulnerability details

## Summary

`RestakeManager.calculateTVLs()` calculates incorrect amount of TVL.

## Impact

Calculating totalWithdrawalQueueValue for incorrect token can lead to different TVL than it's supposed to be which may result in getting different amount of shares. Can be can be negative for the user (if price of `collateralTokens[i]` is greater than `collateralTokens[j]`) or can be negatve for the protocol (if price of `collateralTokens[i]` is smaller than `collateralTokens[j]`).

## Proof of Concept

Values returned from `RestakeManager.calculateTVLs()` areused in taking calculation of how many shares would be minted/burned to user.
However, when this function calculates value of tokens (in ETH) in `WithdrawQueue` it gets incorrect address of token to get value for.

```solidity
    // record token value of withdraw queue
    if (!withdrawQueueTokenBalanceRecorded) {
        totalWithdrawalQueueValue += renzoOracle.lookupTokenValue(
@>          collateralTokens[i],
            collateralTokens[j].balanceOf(withdrawQueue)
        );
    }
```

Instead of getting value of token in current loop iteration, it gets token value of incorrect `collateralTokens[i]`. In this case index `i` is always `0` because it's index from outer loop. That means it calculates token value of first token with amount of token it should have been calculated. `RestakeManager.calculateTVLs()` is used in `RestakeManager.deposit()`, `RestakeManager.depositETH()`, `RestakeManager.depositTokenRewardsFromProtocol()`, `BalancerRateProvider.getRate()`, `WithdrawQueue.withdraw()` which are main fund flow functions and they are dependent on correct return value from `RestakeManager.calculateTVLs()`.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Get collateral token from array by correct index:

```diff
@@ -315,7 +315,7 @@ contract RestakeManager is Initializable, ReentrancyGuardUpgradeable, RestakeMan
    // record token value of withdraw queue
    if (!withdrawQueueTokenBalanceRecorded) {
        totalWithdrawalQueueValue += renzoOracle.lookupTokenValue(
-           collateralTokens[i],
+           collateralTokens[j],
            collateralTokens[j].balanceOf(withdrawQueue)
        );
    }
```


## Assessed type

Loop

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L472


# Vulnerability details


## Impact
There's a problem with the gas refund functionality in the `OperatorDelegator` contract when the `NativeEthRestakeAdmin` is a contract account.
The `_recordGas` function is using `msg.sender` to track gas spending.
But `tx.origin` is used to refund gas in the `_refundGas` function.
So when the admin is a contract account (`msg.sender` will be different from `tx.origin`), the gas refund won't work.

## Proof of Concept
[_recordGas](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L470~L474)
[_refundGas](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L481~L493)

contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L509
```solidity
    if (adminGasSpentInWei[tx.origin] > 0) { // @audit tx.origin != msg.sender?
        gasRefunded = _refundGas();
        // update the remaining amount
        remainingAmount -= gasRefunded;
        // If no funds left, return
        if (remainingAmount == 0) {
            return;
        }
    }
```

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
To fix this issue, it's recommended to use the `tx.origin` instead of `msg.sender` to track gas spending.






## Assessed type

ETH-Transfer

# Vulnerability details


## Impact
This incorrect token balance will affect the `calculateTVLs` calculation so that the TVLs will be incorrect.
All operations relying on calculateTVLs, such as deposits and withdrawals, will be based on faulty data.

## Proof of Concept

The `queuedShares` is updated in the `queueWithdrawals` and `completeQueuedWithdrawl` function.
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L231~L232

```solidity
    // track shares of tokens withdraw for TVL
    queuedShares[address(tokens[i])] += queuedWithdrawalParams[0].shares[i];
```

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L280~L281

```solidity
    queuedShares[address(tokens[i])] -= withdrawal.shares[i];
```

```solidity
    function getTokenBalanceFromStrategy(IERC20 token) external view returns (uint256) {
```

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Bridge/L2/Oracle/RenzoOracleL2.sol#L51


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
To ensure reliable data in L2 environments like Arbitrum, Chainlink integrations must include checks for sequencer health. This prevents oracles from relying on potentially inaccurate information during sequencer downtime.
This will affect the depositing of tokens in `xRenzoDeposit` contract.

## Proof of Concept
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Bridge/L2/Oracle/RenzoOracleL2.sol#L50~L57
```solidity
    function getMintRate() public view returns (uint256, uint256) {
        (, int256 price, , uint256 timestamp, ) = oracle.latestRoundData(); //@audit missing sequencer checking
        if (timestamp < block.timestamp - MAX_TIME_WINDOW) revert OraclePriceExpired(); // @audit price > 0?
        // scale the price to have 18 decimals
        uint256 _scaledPrice = (uint256(price)) * 10 ** (18 - oracle.decimals());
        if (_scaledPrice < 1 ether) revert InvalidOraclePrice();
        return (_scaledPrice, timestamp);
    }
```

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
It's recommended to implement the sequencer checking by following this: https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/l2-sequencer-feeds#example-code




## Assessed type

Oracle


## Tools Used
Manual review

To enable pausing `withdraw` and `claim` in emergency situations, it's recommended to incorporate the `whenNotPaused` modifier to both functions.

raw_row.title: Incorrect Updates to stakedButNotVerifiedEth May Result in an Inflated TVL

title: Incorrect Updates to stakedButNotVerifiedEth May Result in an Inflated TVL
warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L381-L389


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
In `OperatorDelegator.sol`, `stakedButNotVerifiedEth` is used to track how much ETH has been sent to the Deposit contract but has not yet been verified by EigenPod. 

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L358

The function `verifyWithdrawalCredentials` deducts the effective balance of validators from `stakedButNotVerifiedEth`, typically 32 ETH. 

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L381-L389

However, this function does not account for the possibility that a validator's effective balance might be reduced below 32 ETH due to penalties, leading to an inflated calculation of the Total Value Locked (TVL).

## Proof of Concept
1. Assume that 32 ETH are deposited into the Deposit contract, setting `stakedButNotVerifiedEth` to 32 ETH.
2. A validator is penalized by the consensus mechanism, reducing their effective balance to 30 ETH.
3. When updated via `verifyWithdrawalCredentials`, only 30 ETH which is the validator's effective balance are deducted from `stakedButNotVerifiedEth`.
4. As a result, `getStakedETHBalance` function would incorrectly return 30 ETH (Pod Owner Shares) + 2 ETH (stakedButNotVerifiedEth), instead of 30 ETH.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L338-L345

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
In the `verifyWithdrawalCredentials` function, `stakedButNotVerifiedEth` should be deducted by 32 ETH instead of the effective balance.


## Assessed type

Context

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L315-L321
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L564-L569
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L605-L609
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L355


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
When users apply for a withdrawal, they deposit ezETH into the `WithdrawQueue`. In `RestakeManager.sol`, the function `renzoOracle.calculateMintAmount` calculates how much new ezETH to mint, taking into account the ezETH in the `WithdrawQueue`, and `calculateTVLs()` also accounts for the collateral in the WithdrawQueue.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L605-L609

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L315-L321

The issue here is that the exchange ratio between ezETH and collateral is fixed at the time of withdrawal application. Any rewards earned by the protocol after this application do not affect this ratio. However, including these deposited ezETH in the TVL calculation can dilute subsequent users' staking rewards and can be manipulated to influence the price of ezETH.

Based on this vulnerability, an further attack scenario can be constructed, assuming the protocol's TVL is initially 0:
1. An attacker deposits ETH and immediately applies for a withdrawal without claiming it.
2. A victim deposits ETH, earning staking rewards for the protocol.
3. The attacker deposits more ETH and immediately executes the claim from step (1).

Through this attack process, the attacker can realize an instant profit in step three, derived from the staking rewards earned by the victim.

## Proof of Concept
https://gist.github.com/StillFantastic/26338c38774d9e1dfe87d2420737c010

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
In the `calculateTVLs` function of `RestakeManager.sol`, the calculation should exclude `claimReserve` from the `WithdrawQueue`, and the total supply of ezETH should also deduct the ezETH in the WithdrawQueue.





## Assessed type

Context

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
In `RestakeManager.sol`, the `calculateTVLs()` function includes the amount of Ether in the `DepositQueue` contract when calculating the TVL. This calculation is used to determine the price of ezETH, providing an opportunity for the protocol's first staker to manipulate the price of ezETH.

raw_row.title: `getAvailableToWithdraw` Can Revert for Assets Like stETH Due to Their Rebase Mechanism

title: `getAvailableToWithdraw` Can Revert for Assets Like stETH Due to Their Rebase Mechanism
warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L156-L162


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
`WithdrawQueue` uses the `getAvailableToWithdraw` function to calculate the current amount available for withdrawal. Amounts that have been applied for withdrawal but not yet claimed are recorded in `claimReserve` and are deducted from the contract’s balance.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L156-L162

However, for rebase tokens like stETH, which uses shares for the underlying accounting, it's possible for the balance of an address's stETH to decrease if there is a loss in the Lido protocol. In scenarios where most of the stETH in the `WithdrawQueue` has been applied for withdrawal, the calculation of balance minus `claimReserve` could be very close or equal to zero. If the stETH balance then decreases, this could cause the contract to experience an underflow error.

Since the protocol's minting and withdrawal functions both use the `getAvailableToWithdraw` function, if such a situation occurs, both minting and withdrawal functionalities will become unusable.

## Proof of Concept
https://gist.github.com/StillFantastic/5ff507216f55427052b3755c3d217ea0

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
It is recommended to add an additional check in `getAvailableToWithdraw` to return zero directly when the balance is less than `claimReserve`.


## Assessed type

DoS

title: TVL Calculation Should Deduct `adminGasSpentInWei`
warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L501-L526
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L470-L474
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L274-L358


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
`adminGasSpentInWei` is recorded in the `OperatorDelegator` contract to track the amount of gas fees spent by the admin. It is deducted from staking rewards when they are transferred from the `DelayedWithdrawalRouter` to the `OperatorDelegator` contract and paid to the admin. Thus, `adminGasSpentInWei` can be considered a liability of the protocol.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L470-L474

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L501-L526

It is noted that `adminGasSpentInWei` increases with each admin operation, yet staking rewards might only be withdrawn occasionally. Therefore, when calculating the protocol's TVL in `RestakeManager` through `calculateTVLs`, it is essential to deduct `adminGasSpentInWei`. Otherwise, uninformed users might mint ezETH without awareness of this fee, and when staking rewards are withdrawn, the TVL could suddenly drop, leading to losses.

## Proof of Concept

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
It is recommended that the calculation of TVL should deduct `adminGasSpentInWei` in the `OperatorDelegator` to accurately reflect the protocol's true TVL.


## Assessed type

Context

raw_row.title: RestakeManager susceptible to an inflation attack

title: RestakeManager susceptible to an inflation attack
warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Oracle/RenzoOracle.sol#L123-L149


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
First depositor can inflate the exchange rate of ezETH token such that any user who deposits afterwards receives less ezETH tokens for their deposits than they should. More info [here](https://mixbytes.io/blog/overview-of-the-inflation-attack), check example 2. 

## Proof of Concept
RestakeManager accepts ETH and ERC20 both as a collateral for minting ezETH token. Both could be used to perform this attack, however for simplicity, I'm going to show it for ETH deposits. 

Let's have a look at the formula that is used to calculate the `ezETHToMint`, 
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L605-L609

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Oracle/RenzoOracle.sol#L123-L149

```solidity
        uint256 inflationPercentaage = (SCALE_FACTOR * _newValueAdded) /
            (_currentValueInProtocol + _newValueAdded);

        // Calculate the new supply
        uint256 newEzETHSupply = (_existingEzETHSupply * SCALE_FACTOR) /
            (SCALE_FACTOR - inflationPercentaage);

        // Subtract the old supply from the new supply to get the amount to mint
        uint256 mintAmount = newEzETHSupply - _existingEzETHSupply;
```
The mintAmount is determined by subtracting `_existingEzETHSupply` from the `newEzETHSupply`, since those value already calculated above, we can simplified it futher for better view. 

```solidity
	// looks familiar
        uint256 mintAmount = (_newValueAdded * _existingEzETHSupply) / _currentValueInProtocol; 

```

the _existingEzETHSupply and _currentValueInProtocol(e.g. tvl) intiallialy are 0, 

To perform an attack; 
- An attacker deposit 1 wei of ETH via depositETH(), since _existingEzETHSupply=0, the `ezETHToMint` is same as 1 wei
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Oracle/RenzoOracle.sol#L130-L132
```solidity
        if (_currentValueInProtocol == 0 || _existingEzETHSupply == 0) {
            return _newValueAdded; // value is priced in base units, so divide by scale factor
        }
```
- another `depositETH()` txn sent by a legimate user with 2 ETH of assets. Attacker saw it and try to frontrun it by a `depositQueue.forwardFullWithdrawalETH(1 ether)` call,  

Note here, we cannot directly sent 1 ETH to depositQueue, since receive() will triggered and charge fee on the attacker sent amount. 

The `forwardFullWithdrawalETH()` function here doing same as direct deposit will, also this call fill the withdraw buffer if required(means sending required fraction to withdrawQueue), but that won't be a problem, we'll see ahead.

- For victim during it deposits, 

_newValueAdded          = 2 ETH, 
_existingEzETHSupply    = 1 WEI, 
_currentValueInProtocol = totalTVL

totalTVL is retrieved from `calculateTVLs()` function during the deposits, it can seen below that the totalTVL includes eth balance from depositQueue and withdrawQueue(which possibly filled during `forwardFullWithdrawalETH` call above) contract as well, 
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L351-L356
```solidity
        // Get the value of native ETH held in the deposit queue and add it to the total TVL
        totalTVL += address(depositQueue).balance;

        // Add native ETH help in withdraw Queue and totalWithdrawalQueueValue to totalTVL
        totalTVL += (address(withdrawQueue).balance + totalWithdrawalQueueValue);

```

So the totalTVL = 1 wei + 1 ETH from attacker

Due to rounding, the victim gets `(2 ether * 1) / (1 ether + 1) == 1 shares` which is same amount as the attacker. Attacker manage to steal `(3 ether / 2) - 1 ether == 0.5 ether` worth of extra shares from the victim. 
```solidity
        uint256 mintAmount = (_newValueAdded * _existingEzETHSupply) / _currentValueInProtocol; 
```

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
There are few mitigation strategies shared [here](https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts/issues/3706#issuecomment-1297199749), which could be implemented by Renzo.



## Assessed type

ERC4626

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L279


# Vulnerability details


## Impact
Renzo does support a blacklist token, e.g., wBETH. If a user is added to the blacklist during the cooldown period, they will not be able to claim wBETH, as it is transferred back to the same blacklisted address.

https://etherscan.io/token/0xa2E3356610840701BDf5611a53974510Ae27E2e1#writeProxyContract#F2

## Proof of Concept

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L318


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

`RestakeManager::calculateTVLs()` is used for rate calculation throughout the protocol, incorrect tvls return by it could be disaster to the protocol. 

While calculating the value holded by WithdrawQueue through `lookupTokenValue()`, it uses index `i` instead of `j`, meaning it passes the same collateral address during the for-loop but differnt balance(which are correponding to other collateralTokens) to get the value. As a result, `totalWithdrawalQueueValue` recorded wrong token value from the withdrawQueue, which later added to `totalTVL`. 

## Proof of Concept
There are many instances. I'll cover one of them, which uses this `totalTVL` to calculate the mintRate for `xezETH` token on L2.  

BalancerRateProvide uses the current `totalTVL` to return the ezETH price in ETH via getRate(), 
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RateProvider/BalancerRateProvider.sol#L29-L41

this function is utilized by `xRenzoBridge::sendPrice()` to send the price as a exchangeRate to the `CCIPReceiver` contract on L2, 
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Bridge/L1/xRenzoBridge.sol#L215-L216

where the receiver contract, further calls `xRenzoDeposit.updatePrice(_price,)` to reflect the latest ezETH price from L1
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Bridge/L2/PriceFeed/CCIPReceiver.sol#L77

And finally, the `xRenzoDeposit::deposit()` utilized those received price to calculate the xezETH mintAmount. 
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Bridge/L2/xRenzoDeposit.sol#L245


## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Change collateralTokens[i] -> collateralTokens[j] [here](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L318),
```diff
        totalWithdrawalQueueValue += renzoOracle.lookupTokenValue(
-	    collateralTokens[i],
+           collateralTokens[j],
            collateralTokens[j].balanceOf(withdrawQueue)
        );
```

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Deposits/DepositQueue.sol#L158-L163


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

When the protocol receive rewards from the EigenLayer, those rewards for ex. native ETH is channelled to the DepositQueue contract through the rewardHandler, increasing the totalTVL currently hold by the protocol. Since ezETH supply is backed by the totalTVL, any ezETH token holder receive more value for their shares as the more value get added to the protocol. 

Before rewards get add to the totalTVL, an attacker could take advantage by frontrunning it with the deposit txn in RestakeManager(which mints ezETH token shares to the attacker) , and immediately backrunning it with `withdrawQueue::withdraw()` request. 

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L220-L224
```solidity
    function withdraw(uint256 _amount, address _assetOut) external nonReentrant {
        // transfer ezETH tokens to this address
        IERC20(address(ezETH)).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), _amount);

        // calculate totalTVL
        (, , uint256 totalTVL) = restakeManager.calculateTVLs();

        // Calculate amount to Redeem in ETH
        uint256 amountToRedeem = renzoOracle.calculateRedeemAmount(
            _amount,
            ezETH.totalSupply(),
            totalTVL
        );
	...snip...
    }
```


Notice the `amountToRedeem` above calculated from the new `totalTVL`. As a result, attacker manage to steal more value out of the protocol, griefing the other stakers with less rewards.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Oracle/RenzoOracle.sol#L157-L158

An epoch system could be built around withdrawQueue, where the ezETH holders eligible for new rewards if only if they have staked previously.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L280-L281


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
[DelegationManager.undelegate()](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/eigenlayer-contracts/blob/15b679b08e7a3589ff83a5e84076ca4e0a00ec0b/src/contracts/core/DelegationManager.sol#L211) can be called by a staker to undelegate themselves, or by a staker's delegated operator, where the staker here is the Renzo `OperatorDelegator`. Undelegation lead to [queue withdrawals](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/eigenlayer-contracts/blob/15b679b08e7a3589ff83a5e84076ca4e0a00ec0b/src/contracts/core/DelegationManager.sol#L678) on behalf of the staker for all their delegated shares. They are removed from the StrategyManager while the withdrawal is in the queue. After a delay period, this withdrawal can be completed by the staker by calling the `completeQueueWithdrawal` on `DelegationManager`. 

In Renzo, generally the nativeEthRestakeAdmin calls the `OperatorDelegator.completeQueuedWithdrawal()` function to complete any queued withdrawals. However, the issue is that this function on `OperatorDelegator` is only eligible to complete withdrawals queued from within Renzo. Any withdrawal queued outside of Renzo cannot be completed.

As a result, there will be a significant drop in Renzo's total TVL. The exchange rate, which is dependent on the total TVL, will be further reduced, directly affecting any withdrawal of LRT tokens via the `WithdrawQueue`.

## Proof of Concept
A mapping `queuedShares` is used to [add](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L232)/[subtract](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L281) respective tokenAmount during queueWithdrawals/completeQueuedWithdrawal, 

```solidity
abstract contract OperatorDelegatorStorageV4 is OperatorDelegatorStorageV3 {
    /// @dev mapping of token shares in withdraw queue of EigenLayer
    mapping(address => uint256) public queuedShares;
}
```

if withdrawal get queued outside the Renzo, the `queuedShares` mapping will left empty for the respective token. And when the nativeEthRestakeAdmin try to `completeQueuedWithdrawal` on `OperatorDelegator` its reverts, since its trying to deduct the `queuedShares` which never got added via the OperatorDelegator. 

```solidty
            // deduct queued shares for tracking TVL
            queuedShares[address(tokens[i])] -= withdrawal.shares[i];
```

The subtraction above will underflow, the `completeQueuedWithdrawal` txn will revert. The nativeEthRestakeAdmin unable to withdraw their stuck funds on the Eigenlayer strategies. 
## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
If it possible anyhow to sync the `queuedShares` with the amount actually queued on EigenLayer protocol, the sync method can be added to OperatorDelegator. If not, we can add a check to deduct queued shares only when `queuedShares[address(tokens[i])] > 0 && queuedShares[address(tokens[i])] > withdrawal.shares[i]`.
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/519e518f2d8dec9acf6482b84a181e403070d22d/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L281


## Assessed type

DoS
