# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L501


# Vulnerability details

It's impossible to withdraw ETH from Eigenlayer because [OperatorDelegator::completeQueuedWithdrawal()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L265) will always revert due to `nonReentrant` modifiers.

When completing a withdrawal for ETH the function [OperatorDelegator::completeQueuedWithdrawal()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L265) needs to be called, which will internally perform the following calls:

1. [DelegationManager::completeQueuedWithdrawal()](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/eigenlayer-contracts/blob/mainnet/src/contracts/core/DelegationManager.sol#L323)
2. [EigenPodManager::withdrawSharesAsTokens()](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/eigenlayer-contracts/blob/mainnet/src/contracts/pods/EigenPodManager.sol#L221)
3. [EigenPod::withdrawRestakedBeaconChainETH()](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/eigenlayer-contracts/blob/mainnet/src/contracts/pods/EigenPod.sol#L431)
4. [OperatorDelegator::receive()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L501)

The call flow starts and ends in the same contract: `OperatorDelegator`. Both the functions [OperatorDelegator::completeQueuedWithdrawal()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L265) and [OperatorDelegator::receive()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L501) have a `nonReentrant` modifier, which will make the call revert.

## Impact

ETH can't be withdrawn from Eigenlayer to Renzo, making it impossible for stakers to exchange their `ezETH` for `ETH`.

## Proof of Concept

It's possible to verify this by following the flow outlined above. Note that the function `EigenPod::withdrawRestakedBeaconChainETH()`(`4`) transfers `ETH` to the `EigenPod` owner, which is the `OperatorDelegator` of which the `receive()` function will be triggered.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Remove the `nonReentrant` modifer from the [OperatorDelegator::receive()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L501) function.


## Assessed type

DoS

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Bridge/L1/xRenzoBridge.sol#L139


# Vulnerability details

The protocol allows to deposit `ETH`/`WETH` (or the specific chain native currency) on a supported L2 in order to mint `ezETH` tokens, this is the process:

1. User mints `xezETH` on L2s via [xRenzoDeposit::deposit()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Bridge/L2/xRenzoDeposit.sol#L204) in exchange for either `ETH` or `WETH`. The `xezETH` are minted based on the **current** `ezETH` valuation.
2. After some time the bridge sweepers transfer the `ETH`/`WETH` collected to the L1, via [xRenzoDeposit::sweep()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Bridge/L2/xRenzoDeposit.sol#L414). The funds are transferred to the `xRenzoBridge` contract on L1 via Connext.
3. Connext calls [xRenzoBridge::xReceive()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Bridge/L1/xRenzoBridge.sol#L139) on L1 which will receive the `ETH`/`WETH` and deposit them in the protocol via [RestakeManager::depositETH()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L592). This will mint `ezETH` tokens based on the **current** `ezETH` valuation, the `ezETH` tokens will then be locked in the lockbox in exchange for `xezETH`, which are then immediately burned because an equivalent amount should have already been minted on the L2 during step `1`.

Theoretically the amount of `xezETH` tokens minted during step `1` should be the same as the amount of `ezETH` tokens minted during step `3`, but because on both steps the tokens are minted at the current valuation, and the valuation changes over time, there will be a discrepancy between the amount of `xezETH` and `ezETH` tokens in circulation. 

This is an issue because [XERC20Lockbox::withdraw()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Bridge/xERC20/contracts/XERC20Lockbox.sol#L126-L135) always exchanges `xezETH` for `ezETH` 1:1.

## Impact

The price of `ezETH` is expected to increase over time. This will create a situation where there will be more `xezETH` in circulation than `ezETH`, rendering some `xezETH` worthless and impossible to redeem for `ezETH`.

A situation in which the `ezETH` valuation decreases instead of increasing is also problematic, because the protocol will mint less `xezETH` than it should.

The discrepancy will become bigger and bigger with time.

## Proof of Concept

As an example, let's assume `ezETH` valuation is currently `1 ETH`:

1. Alice deposits `1 ETH` on L2 and receives `1 xezETH`
2. Some time passes and the valuation of `ezETH` increases to `2ETH` (unrealistic, but allows simple math)
3. The bridge sweeper calls `sweep()`, transferring the `1 ETH` to the `xRenzoBridge` contract on L1
4. The `xRenzoBridge` deposits the received `1 ETH` in the `RestakeManager`, which mints `0.5 ezETH` because the `ezETH` valuation doubled
5. The `0.5 ezETH` is locked in the lockbox, `0.5 xezETH` are minted in return and immediately burned

The situation now is the following:

- Alice has `1 xezETH` on L2
- The lockbox contains `0.5 ezETH` on L1

Alice can at best redeem `0.5 xezETH` in exchange for `0.5 ezETH`, and the remaning `0.5 xezETH` is worthless. The amount of value she can redeem is the correct one, (`1 ETH`), but now there are `xezETH` in circulation that are not backed by `ezETH`.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

The protocol should track the amount of `xezETH` tokens minted via [xRenzoDeposit::deposit()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Bridge/L2/xRenzoDeposit.sol#L204) on the L2 and mint the equivalent amount of `ezETH` tokens on L1 when [xRenzoBridge::xReceive()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Bridge/L1/xRenzoBridge.sol#L139) is executed by passing the necessary data on the [xcall()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Bridge/L2/xRenzoDeposit.sol#L434-L442) to Connext.

If this is implemented it's possible for the valuation of `ezETH` tokens to change instantly after [xRenzoBridge::xReceive()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Bridge/L1/xRenzoBridge.sol) is executed, this is because the amount of `ezETH` tokens is not minted based on the current valuation anymore. As explained in other reports, the protocol will be subject to instant `ezETH` valuation changes (increase/decrease) no matter what (rewards, slashing, penalties), and should gracefully handle these situations via appropriate deposit and withdrawals queues.


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L364


# Vulnerability details

A validator staked balance can drop (slashing, penalties) while it's balance not yet verified on Eigenlayer. If this happens the protocol will not account for the losses.

Staking ETH to an operator validator requires two steps:

1. An admin calls [DepositQueue::stakeEthFromQueue()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Deposits/DepositQueue.sol#L187):
    1. `32 ETH` are deposited in the validator
    2. The `stakedButNotVerifiedEth` variable is [increased by `32 ETH`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L358)

2. An admin calls [OperatorDelegator::verifyWithdrawalCredentials()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L364):
    1. The `stakeButNotVerifiedEth` variable is decreased by the [current effective balance of the validator](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L385)

There is a timeframe between step `1` and step `2` in which the validator could receive penalties or could be slashed. In step `2` the variable `stakeButNotVerifiedEth` will only be lowered by the current effective balance of the validator, but the variable was increased by `32ETH` during step`1`. Because the variable is used in the [TVL calculation](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L343-L344), and was not properly lowered by `32ETH`, the protocol will consider the TVL to be higher than it actually is.

## Impact

The TVL will be considered higher than it actually is by the protocol, making some `ezETH` impossible to redeem for `ETH` because those `ETH` don't exist.

## Proof of Concept

1. An admin calls [DepositQueue::stakeEthFromQueue()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Deposits/DepositQueue.sol#L187) to deposit `32ETH` into Alice validator
2. Alice validator receives some penalties, reducing the validator balance to `31ETH`
3. An admin calls [OperatorDelegator::verifyWithdrawalCredentials()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L364), this will lower the `stakeButNotVerifiedEth` variable to `1ETH` and set the `podOwnerShares[]` [variable on Eigenlayer](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/eigenlayer-contracts/blob/mainnet/src/contracts/pods/EigenPodManager.sol#L118) to `31 ETH`.

Because both `podOwnerShares[]` (`31 ETH`) and `stakeButNotVerifiedEth` (`1 ETH`) are used in the TVL calculations, the protocol will consider the TVL to be equal to `32ETH` but the TVL should be `31ETH`.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Always lower the `stakeButNotVerifiedEth` by `32ETH` when executing [OperatorDelegator::verifyWithdrawalCredentials()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L364). In case this fix is implemented and the situation described in the report happens, the TVL will instantly drop. The protocol should be able to handle instant TVL drops by implementing a proper withdrawal queue.


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Oracle/RenzoOracle.sol#L123


# Vulnerability details

The function [RenzoOracle::calculateMintAmount()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Oracle/RenzoOracle.sol#L123) is used by the protocol to calculate the amount of `ezETH` to mint based on the TVL and the amount of assets deposited, but doesn't implement a virtual shares system to prevent inflation attacks.

If the protocol TVL or the amount of `ezETH` in circulation is currently `0` an attacker can monitor the mempool for a deposit and frontrun it for profit.

## Impact

An attacker can frontrun a deposit for profit when the protocol TVL or the amount of `ezETH` is `0`.

## Proof of Concept

Let's assume Alice is performing the first the deposit of `1 ETH`, an attacker monitoring the mempool notices this and he:

1. Deposits `1 wei` via [RestakeManager::depositETH()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L592), which will mint `1 wei` of `ezETH`.
2. Send `0.5 ETH` directly to the protocol, as a donation. This will increase the TVL and `1 wei` of `ezETH` will now be worth `0.5 ETH + 1 wei`.
3. The deposit that got frontrun goes through, Alice is supposed to receive `1.99 wei` of `ezETH` but due to precision loss she will only receive `1 wei` of `ezETH`.

The current state of the protocol is:

- TVL: `1 ETH` + `0.5ETH` + `1 wei` = `1.5ETH` + `1 wei`
- `ezETH` in circulation: `2 wei`

This implies `1 wei` of `ezETH` is valued at ~`1.5ETH / 2` = `0.75ETH`. The attacker can now withdraw his `1 wei` of `ezETH` for a profit of ~`0.25ETH` (`0.75ETH` - `0.5ETH`).

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Implement a virtual shares system, like [openzeppelin does for ERC4626 vaults](https://docs.openzeppelin.com/contracts/4.x/erc4626#defending_with_a_virtual_offset).


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L299
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L303


# Vulnerability details

Executing [WithdrawQueue::claim()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L279) to complete the withdrawal process will almost always lead to instant changes in `ezETH` valuation.

Redeeming `ezETH` for underlying assets involves two steps:

1. User calls [WithdrawQueue::withdraw()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L206), which:
    1. Transfers `ezETH` from the caller to the contract
    2. Caches the amount of assets to redeem based on the **current** `ezETH` valuation
2. After a delay, the user can call [WithdrawQueue::claim()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L279), which:
    1. Burns the amount of `ezETH` previously transferred
    2. Transfers to the caller the amount of assets to redeem cached during step `1`

Because there is an uncapped delay in between step `1` and step `2`, when step `2` is executed the amount of `ezETH` burned might not be equivalent to the assets transferred out anymore, which will cause an instant change in the `ezETH` valuation.

## Impact

The valuation of `ezETH` should not increase (or decrease) instantly because this is not a situation where the protocol is receiving rewards (or penalties).

The instant increase of `ezETH` value can be abused by an attacker by depositing `ETH` in the protocol via [RestakeManager::depositETH()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L592) before a call to [WithdrawQueue::claim()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L279) and withdrawing after the call.

Important to note that the delay between a call to `withdraw()` and `claim()` is uncapped and can be very long.

## Proof of Concept

Let's assume the protocol TVL is `2 ETH` and there are a total of `2 ezETH` in circulation, which implies `1 ezETH` is valued at `1 ETH`.

1. Alice calls [WithdrawQueue::withdraw()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L206) to redeem `1 ezETH`, the protocol caches the current equivalent amount to be redeemed, `1 ETH`.
2. In between the calls the TVL of the protocol increases while the amount of `ezETH` in circulation stays constant, due to rewards. Let's assume the TVL doubled and is now `4 ETH` (unrealistic, but simple math).
3. Alice calls [WithdrawQueue::claim()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L279), which burns `1 ezETH` and transfers out `1 ETH`.

Before step `3` was executed the protocol state was:

- `4 ETH` TVL
- `2 ezETH` in circulation
- `1 ezETH` = `2 ETH`

After step `3` is executed the protocol state is:

- `3 ETH` TVL
- `1 ezETH` in circulation
- `1 ezETH` = `3 ETH`

The valuation of `ezETH` instantly increased by `1ETH` after `claim()` was executed.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

When [WithdrawQueue::withdraw()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L206) is executed the protocol should:

1. Burn the transferred `ezETH` tokens
2. Don't account for the amount of assets that will be redeemed as part of the TVL. They can be sent to an external contract that is responsible to keep the funds until they are claimed via [WithdrawQueue::claim()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L279).

If this is implemented calls to [WithdrawQueue::claim()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L279) will have no impact on the `ezETH` valuation, because both the amount of `ezETH` and the TVL won't change after the call.


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L529-L530


# Vulnerability details

The protocol allows to set caps to the amount of tokens that can be deposited. The function [RestakeManager::deposit()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L529-L530) is responsible for making sure these caps are respected:

```solidity
// Enforce individual token TVL limit if set, 0 means the check is not enabled
if (collateralTokenTvlLimits[_collateralToken] != 0) {
    ...SNIP...
    // Check if it is over the limit
@>  if (currentTokenTVL + collateralTokenValue > collateralTokenTvlLimits[_collateralToken])
        revert MaxTokenTVLReached();
}
```

The sum `currentTokenTVL + collateralTokenValue`, used to check if the max TVL cap per token is reached, doesn't include tokens [currently sitting in the `WithdrawQueue`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L316-L321), which are generally [accounted for as TVL by the protocol](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L317-L320).

The `currentTokenTVL` variable only includes the value of tokens currently held as shares by `OperatorDelegator(s)` (including shares in the process of being withdrawn), this can be verified in [RestakeManager::calculateTVLs()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L302-L304), which calls into [OperatorDelegator::getTokenBalanceFromStrategy()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Delegation/OperatorDelegator.sol#L327):

```solidity
function getTokenBalanceFromStrategy(IERC20 token) external view returns (uint256) {
    return
        queuedShares[address(this)] == 0
            ? tokenStrategyMapping[token].userUnderlyingView(address(this))
            : tokenStrategyMapping[token].userUnderlyingView(address(this)) +
                tokenStrategyMapping[token].sharesToUnderlyingView(
                    queuedShares[address(token)]
                );
}
```

## Impact

The protocol can accept more tokens than expected.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

In [RestakeManager::deposit()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/RestakeManager.sol#L529-L530) account for the tokens currently held in the `WithdrawQueue` when checking if the token TVL maximum cap has been reached.


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L214


# Vulnerability details

The `ezETH` token is supposed to be non-transferrable in early stages of the protocol, but [WithdrawQueue::withdraw()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/Withdraw/WithdrawQueue.sol#L214) tries to transfer `ezETH` from the user to the `WithdrawQueue` contract:
```solidity
    function withdraw(uint256 _amount, address _assetOut) external nonReentrant {
        ...SNIP...
        IERC20(address(ezETH)).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), _amount);
        ...SNIP...
    }
```

this will always revert when `ezETH` is non-transferrable.

## Impact

Users can't redeem their `ezETH` for tokens/ETH when `ezETH` transfers are not enabled. This is not supposed to be the case:
> When the protocol launches, it is intended to not have ezETH be transferrable. A user will deposit and get ezETH minted to their account, but they will not be able to transfer it out of their account until the protocol is ready to allow it. If the withdrawal flow is enabled, they can still withdraw from the protocol (token can be minted and burned by RestakeManager, even if transfers are restricted).

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Change the [EzEthToken::_beforeTokenTransfer()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-04-renzo/blob/main/contracts/token/EzEthToken.sol#L56) function to always allow the `WithdrawQueue` contract to transfer `ezETH`:

```solidity
...SNIP
if (from != address(0) && to != address(0) && msg.sender != withdrawQueue) {
    revert ContractPaused();
}
...SNIP
```


## Assessed type

DoS
